title: Precision Growth
author: Chris M.
desc:
Precision Growth

Precision Growth is a hypertrophy-focused training program designed to maximise muscle growth through intelligent exercise selection, controlled execution, deep loaded stretches, and targeted muscular tension.

The objective is not to lift the most weight, but to create the highest-quality growth stimulus in the target muscle while minimising unnecessary joint stress, systemic fatigue, and recovery demands. Every exercise, set, and repetition has a purpose.

Built around an Upper/Lower structure with dedicated refinement work, Precision Growth prioritises sustainable progress, long-term joint health, and the development of a balanced, aesthetic physique.

Precision Growth Principles
1. Target Muscle First

The goal is to challenge the intended muscle, not simply move the weight from A to B. Exercise execution and muscle recruitment take priority over load.

2. The Stretch Is the Rep

Deep loaded stretches are a cornerstone of the program. Controlled eccentrics and full ranges of motion are used to maximise tension in lengthened muscle positions.

3. Control the Load

Momentum, ego lifting, and compensatory movement patterns are minimised. The lifter controls the weight at all times, particularly during the eccentric phase.

4. Stability Creates Stimulus

Stable exercises allow greater focus on the target muscle. Machines, cables, chest-supported movements, and supported positions are used where they improve stimulus and reduce fatigue.

5. Quality Over Quantity

More volume is not always better. The program emphasises performing fewer sets with greater intent, precision, and effort rather than accumulating unnecessary fatigue.

6. Progress Without Ego

Progressive overload remains essential, but never at the expense of technique. Load is increased only when execution, tempo, and range of motion remain uncompromised.

7. Stimulus-to-Fatigue Ratio Matters

Exercises are selected based on their ability to produce muscle growth while minimising joint stress, recovery cost, and systemic fatigue.

8. Frequency Beats Annihilation

Muscle groups are trained frequently throughout the week using complementary movement patterns rather than relying on excessive volume in a single session.

9. Long-Term Joint Health

The program is designed to support consistent training over years, not weeks. Exercise selection and execution prioritise longevity and resilience.

10. Build the Physique, Then Refine It

The primary training days focus on building muscle, while the Refinement Day addresses areas that benefit from additional frequency and specialised attention, helping create a complete and balanced physique.
